title: Annotatio II §.IX (2): First Institution — body at table, not in bread; else two bodies / self-eating
pass_a_gloss: (2) By the circumstances of the first Institution: For Christ’s Body was then corporally at the table, or reclined corporally at the table, and so was not Corporally in the bread. Likewise, if Christ’s body was then corporally in the bread when Christ, about to institute the Sacrament of the Supper, Himself ate the bread with the disciples (Matt. 26:29; Mark 14:25), it will follow that the same One in and under the bread ate His own flesh; and so then had His whole body and soul in His mouth: hence either a multiplication of the same body of Christ was done, or Christ had two bodies — one containing and eating, the other contained and eaten.
pass_b_english: (2) At the first Institution Christ’s body was corporally at the table — so not corporally in the bread.

If it was in the bread while He Himself ate with the disciples (Matt. 26:29; Mark 14:25), He ate His own flesh in and under the bread — whole body and soul in His mouth — hence either multiplication of one body, or two bodies (one eating, one eaten).
source_text: (2) Circumstantiis primæ Institutionis: Corpus enim Christi fuit tum temporis corporaliter ad mensam, seu mensæ corporaliter accubuit, adeoque Corporaliter in pane non fuit. Item, quòd si corpus Christi corporaliter in pane tum fuit, cùm Christus Sacramentum Coenæ instituturus, ipsemet panem cum discipulis edit. Matth. 26. 29. Marc. 14. 25. sequetur, eundem in & sub pane, suam propriam carnem comedisse; adeoque totum suum corpus & animam, tum temporis in ore habuisse: hincque adeo, vel multiplicationem esse factam ejusdem corporis Christi, vel duo Christum habuisse corpora, unum continens & comedens, alterum contentum & comesum.
